content:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `low_memory_on_detailscreen` (low_memory): Recreate the screen several times, then squeeze memory like a low-RAM phone and come back; destroyed screens must be freed and nothing may crash.
Steps: [{"fault": "recreate_activity", "times": 3}, {"fault": "trim_memory", "level": "RUNNING_CRITICAL"}, {"fault": "trim_memory", "level": "COMPLETE"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: crashed: java.lang.IllegalStateException: FragmentManager has been destroyed
Crash: java.lang.IllegalStateException @ com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.DealLoader$load$1.invokeSuspend(DetailScreen.kt:68)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.DealLoader$load$1.invokeSuspend(DetailScreen.kt:68)

## Diagnosis
Root cause: DetailScreen.kt:79 calls DealLoader.load(activity, ...) from a LaunchedEffect, but DealLoader.load (DetailScreen.kt:62) launches on GlobalScope with Dispatchers.Main. The coroutine outlives the composition and holds the Activity. ProductRepository.byId has a 5 s delay (ProductRepository.kt:52), so after recreate_activity x3 and the trim, the coroutine resumes on a destroyed Activity. It then calls activity.supportFragmentManager.show(...) (DetailScreen.kt:68) on a destroyed FragmentManager, which throws. A second defect keeps the screens alive: MainActivity.kt:32 passes every Activity to ScreenTracker.onScreenCreated, which appends it to a strong-reference list (ScreenTracker.kt:9,13) that is never cleared. That is why a destroyed Activity survives forced GC (activities: 1), and it pins each old Activity's views and fragment manager, which is what the crash then touches.
Fix approach: Run the deal lookup in a scope that is cancelled with the composition (rememberCoroutineScope or LaunchedEffect calling a suspend function) instead of GlobalScope, so a recreated Activity cancels the pending load. Pass the result back to the composable and only show the DealDialogFragment from a live, resumed host, for example by checking lifecycle state before calling show or using lifecycle-aware collection. In ScreenTracker, keep only a count or a WeakReference to the Activity, not a strong list of Activities.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/DetailScreen.kt:62 - GlobalScope.launch(Dispatchers.Main) runs the deal load outside any lifecycle or composition scope; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/DetailScreen.kt:68 - activity.supportFragmentManager.show(...) runs after the coroutine resumes, and crashes with 'FragmentManager has been destroyed' (the reported crash site); app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/DetailScreen.kt:76-79 - the FragmentActivity from LocalContext is captured and passed into the global coroutine by LaunchedEffect; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/data/ProductRepository.kt:52 - byId delays 5000 ms, so the load is still pending when recreate and trim happen; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/analytics/ScreenTracker.kt:9,13 - sessionScreens is a strong MutableList<Activity> that retains every Activity; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:32 - each Activity is registered in ScreenTracker.onScreenCreated(this), which is where the retention starts; memory after forced GC: activities 1 - a destroyed Activity is still alive after GC, consistent with the strong list in ScreenTracker

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/DetailScreen.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/analytics/ScreenTracker.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM test, DealLoaderTest in src/test, that injects the product loader and the deal-popup callback as parameters and a TestScope. The test starts load(scope, loader = { delay(5_000); product }, showDeal = { shown++ }), then cancels the scope (simulating the Activity being destroyed) before advancing time, and asserts showDeal is never invoked and the scope has no active job left. Before the fix this fails because GlobalScope keeps running and calls show. A second test, ScreenTrackerTest, asserts that after onScreenCreated(activity) and the activity is garbage collected, the tracker holds no strong reference to it. Before the fix the strong list keeps it alive.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

44	class DealDialogFragment : DialogFragment() {
45	    override fun onCreateDialog(savedInstanceState: Bundle?): Dialog =
46	        AlertDialog.Builder(requireContext())
47	            .setTitle("Deal unlocked")
48	            .setMessage(requireArguments().getString(ARG_MESSAGE))
49	            .setPositiveButton("Nice", null)
50	            .create()
51	
52	    companion object {
53	        private const val ARG_MESSAGE = "message"
54	        fun newInstance(message: String) = DealDialogFragment().apply { arguments = bundleOf(ARG_MESSAGE to message) }
55	    }
56	}

58	/** Loads a product's detail and announces today's deal in a popup. */
59	@OptIn(DelicateCoroutinesApi::class)
60	object DealLoader {
61	    fun load(activity: FragmentActivity, productId: Int, onLoaded: (Product) -> Unit) {
62	        GlobalScope.launch(Dispatchers.Main) {
63	            val product = ProductRepository.byId(productId)
64	            onLoaded(product)
65	            if (product.dealPercent > 0) {
66	                DealDialogFragment
67	                    .newInstance("${product.dealPercent}% off ${product.name}, today only.")
68	                    .show(activity.supportFragmentManager, "deal")
69	            }
70	        }
71	    }
72	}

content.text:
I replaced the `GlobalScope` launch in `DealLoader.load` with a launch on a scope passed in by the caller. `DetailScreen` now passes its `LaunchedEffect` scope, so recreating the Activity cancels the pending 5 s load. The deal popup is only shown if the Activity is at least STARTED. `ScreenTracker` now keeps just a view count instead of a strong list of Activities, and its `onScreenCreated` parameter is now `Any`. I also removed its `Log.d` call, which would throw in a JVM test.

The regression tests are in `DealLoaderTest`, in `app/src/test`. They cover a cancelled scope never showing the deal, a live scope showing it, and `ScreenTracker` not holding a strong reference. `DealLoaderTest` compiles via the compile tool (`unit`), but I haven't run it. The project has no `kotlinx-coroutines-test`, so it uses a real `CoroutineScope` with short real delays instead of `TestScope`.
